"Thanks for seeing me, Doc. It’s just… things have been a real mess for the past several months, probably since I got divorced. On the road, I used to be sharp, always on schedule. Now, I’m constantly misplacing my logbook or my keys, and it drives me nuts. I’ll get a new route plan, read through it, and then somehow miss a turn or completely forget a delivery stop, causing all sorts of headaches. I used to pride myself on being reliable, but lately, I’m forgetting all sorts of stuff – calls I need to make to dispatch, when bills are due.

My boss has been on my case about not following instructions precisely, and honestly, sometimes it feels like I just can’t keep it all in my head. And to be honest, I just feel… heavy. Like everything takes ten times more effort than it used to. Don't really feel like doing anything when I'm not driving, kinda just sit around. It's been going on for a while now, and I just can't seem to shake it."
D002-D013_h025.question_a:
"Lately, I just can't seem to get things done, doc. My ex-wife always used to say I was spacey, even when I was a kid, always losing my homework or forgetting what the teacher just said. Now, it’s like that but with my trucking routes. I’ll get a dispatch, start driving, and then realize I missed a turn because my mind just drifted off, or worse, I’ll forget my keys or my logbook at the last truck stop. It’s not just the big stuff; it’s the little things too, like forgetting to call my daughter back or missing a bill payment.

And yeah, I've been feeling down, pretty low most days. It’s hard to get motivated, and I just feel tired. But even when I'm feeling alright, not particularly down at all, my brain still feels like it’s in neutral. This isn’t a new thing that just popped up with the sadness; I’ve always struggled with staying focused and remembering things, long before this recent slump started. It’s like the absentmindedness has always been there, just part of me, and the low mood just piled on top."
D002-D013_h025.question_b: "Lately, it's just been a fog. The road used to be a comfort, but now I can barely focus. My ex-wife always complained about my memory, but this is different. It's like my brain just… shuts down. I miss turns, forget where I parked the rig at truck stops, and can't even remember what I ate for breakfast. My dispatcher will give me instructions, and I'll nod along, but then I'm ten minutes down the road, and it's completely gone. I'm losing my logbook, my keys, my wallet – almost lost my CDL last week! This forgetfulness and inability to pay attention, it's really only been this bad for the last six months or so, ever since I started feeling this heavy, sad cloud hanging over me. Before that, sure, I’d misplace things occasionally, but nothing like this."
